audit.whatIsWrong: The shipped chart gives Singed levels 2 and 3 and calls level 6 even, while the entry's own whys say the opposite for all three stages.
audit.why: whys[1] 'he out-trades any melee exchange you try to take', whys[2] 'the lane is his until you can proxy past him', whys[4] 'His Depth Charge interrupts Insanity Potion momentum'. The audit packet levelChart (Skill / Nautilus / Nautilus / Skill / Nautilus / Singed / Singed) matches the prose; the shipped chart does not.
audit.corrected: Level 1 even. Levels 2-3 Nautilus: Dredge Line plus Staggering Blow out-trade you before Mega Adhesive exists. Levels 4-5 even, a proxy standoff. Level 6 Nautilus on Depth Charge. First item onward Singed: 53.33% over 3197 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: content mid tells you to 'track its 90-second cooldown' for Depth Charge.
audit.why: Riot's data gives Depth Charge 120/100/80s. 90 is not one of its ranks, so a player timing a commit off that number is wrong at every level of the ult.
audit.corrected: Depth Charge is 120/100/80s. Dredge Line 14/13/12/11/10s, Titan's Wrath a flat 12s, Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s. Your Insanity Potion is 100s, so at R rank 1 his ult outlasts yours and at rank 3 yours outlasts his.

audit.whatIsWrong: Staggering Blow is described as rooting on every touch, and two of his five abilities never appear at all: Titan's Wrath (W) and Riptide (E).
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Nautilus' first Attack against a target deals increased physical damage and roots them briefly' — once per target, not every auto, so the 'passive-rooted autos' chain in whys[1] and wants.foe[0] does not exist. Titan's Wrath is a flat-12s shield that eats your Fling burst outright. Riptide is a 7s-to-5s triple slow at 600 range and is the single ability that most directly beats Poison Trail, because your damage pattern requires you to be moving.
audit.corrected: His first auto on you roots — one per target, so the second auto is free to walk away from. Force Titan's Wrath out before you commit Fling. Riptide, not the hook, is what kills your run: it slows you three times in a 600 radius on a 7s cooldown, so break line before the second wave lands.

edits.before: Levels 1 through 3 are genuinely rough — Nautilus auto-roots you with his passive every time he touches you, and if he lands Dredge Line you are stuck eating the full melee combo while your Poison Trail does nothing because you are not moving. Do not run at him; instead, push the wave hard at level 1, get the minion bounces, and look to proxy behind the wave by level 4 rather than proving anything in lane. The moment Mega Adhesive comes online you have the fling-root combo, but Nautilus is tanky enough to absorb it at these levels and hook you on the way out — only use it if he overextends without his Q up.
edits.after: Levels 1 through 3 are genuinely rough — Staggering Blow roots you on his first auto against you, once per target, and if he lands Dredge Line you are stuck eating the full melee combo while your Poison Trail does nothing because you are not moving. Do not run at him; instead, push the wave hard at level 1, get the minion bounces, and look to proxy behind the wave by level 4 rather than proving anything in lane. The moment Mega Adhesive comes online you have the fling-root combo, but Nautilus is tanky enough to absorb it at these levels and hook you on the way out — only use it if he overextends without his Q up.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are a farming and proxy window — Nautilus is too slow to catch you if you do not fight him, and you can starve him of CS by running behind his wave and forcing him to choose between you and his minions. At level 6 he gains Depth Charge, a single-target knockup that will end your run pattern cold; track its 90-second cooldown rigorously and commit your Insanity Potion only on the cooldown window. Insanity Potion does not help you win the head-on brawl against a tanky hooked champion — use it to run faster and disengage safely, not to duel him.

notes: Depth Charge's cooldown was wrong in content.mid (90s; Riot's data says 120/100/80s) — a player timing a commit off 90 would be wrong at every rank. Staggering Blow was described as rooting on every auto; Riot's text says first Attack against a target. Both fixed. Riptide (E) and Titan's Wrath (W) were absent from every field despite Riptide being the ability that most directly defeats Poison Trail. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: whether Mega Adhesive's grounding stops Dredge Line's terrain pull. The kit marks the pull with the 'terrain' flag, not 'dash', and whether grounding blocks it is exactly the needsResearch class the brief says not to infer. Left out of the page and raised as a question instead.
